issues.description: The UML/problem statement names the double attribute in ExcellenceLand as 'excellencyLevel' (and thus students will expect a getter named getExcellencyLevel()), but the solution implementation uses a differently named field 'levelOfExcellence' and provides getLevelOfExcellence(). This is an attribute/getter naming mismatch between the specification and the reference solution and may confuse students about the expected attribute/getter names and break automated tests that check exact getter names.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the attribute and its getter name consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to use the attribute name 'excellencyLevel' and provide a getter getExcellencyLevel(), or (B) update the UML/problem statement to use 'levelOfExcellence' and document/getter name getLevelOfExcellence(). Ensure the constructor parameter order and getter names match the chosen attribute name so students and automated tests are aligned.

issues.description: The UML/problem statement declares the ExcellenceLand attribute as 'excellencyLevel' (double), but the solution implementation uses the field name 'levelOfExcellence' and provides getLevelOfExcellence(). This is a naming mismatch for the same conceptual attribute. The exercise instructions require students to create attributes exactly as in the UML and provide corresponding getters; using a different identifier in the solution (and leaving the template empty) creates a mapping mismatch that can confuse students and may cause automated checks that expect the UML name to fail.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the identifier across artifacts. Either (A) rename the solution field and getter to match the UML: change 'private double levelOfExcellence;' to 'private double excellencyLevel;' and provide 'public double getExcellencyLevel()' (and keep the constructor parameter name/order per UML), or (B) update the UML/problem statement to use 'levelOfExcellence' and 'getLevelOfExcellence()' if that name is preferred. Prefer option (A) to follow the current UML wording and the exercise requirements.
